info.album: Free Fire: Original Motion Picture Soundtrack

podcast.body: John Denver wrote this song for his wife, Annie Martell, whom he married in 1967. The inspiration struck him while on a ski lift in Aspen, Colorado, where the mountain's beauty and sensory experience led him to the line "you fill up my senses." He claims to have written the basic melody and lyrics in ten minutes. Though not stylistically closer to country music, its beautiful melody and lyrics about married bliss resonated with both pop and country audiences. By August 1974, it reached number nine on the country chart, marking Denver's first top 10 country hit, and also returned him to number one on the Hot 100. "Denver says, he had written the basic melody and lyrics of a tune that he called Annie's song."

podcast.body: This song was the winner of the 1974 Billboard Song of the Summer. It is a gentle ballad that, despite its win, is noted for not typically sounding like a summer song. It famously held off Paul Anka's "Having My Baby" for the title. "It doesn't sound much like a song of the summer, but it did win for 1974."
